title: Three tests for setting or plot
statement: Count a line in a film before a reading as setting only if it needs no 'then', no character's choice made it true, and it holds without reading the passage.
detail: A reconciliation of a film brief with a research brief on intro videos applied that brief's three tests line by line: a standing test (the line can be said without a 'then'), a cause test (no character's choice inside the passage made it true) and a removal test (it would still be true if the child never read the passage). Words naming standing features of the setting, such as a room, a part of a ship or a kind of weapon, passed all three as world, while a clause saying what one character had done to another failed the cause test and counted as plot, backstory included. The tests serve the side of an unsettled question that keeps plot out of such films.
against: Auto-generated notes of a later meeting, quoted in the same reconciliation, record an agreement to reveal the plot and characters (`grade3-reading/artifacts/video-briefs/PETER-PAN-BRIEF-RECONCILIATION-2026-08-31.md`, lines 228-234), and whether such a film may show plot at all is unsettled.

evidence.quote: **Standing test** — "there is a nursery," "a cutlass is a curved sword," "rigging holds up the masts" are all statements that can be said without a "then." **Cause test** — no character's choice inside the passage makes these words true; they are pre-existing facts about the setting/objects. **Removal test** — nursery/cutlass/hull/rigging would still be true of the world if the child never read the passage.
agreed to reveal the plot and characters, and agreed to start exactly where
